claims.claim: Restored the bounded, versioned, closed-schema checkpoint API with native TASK, ACTIVE RUN, operation, candidate, tree and reviewed-plan bindings.
Checkpoint sealing requires authenticated native execution evidence and complete reviewed proof, independently of plans and Executor claims.
Checkpoint history enforces consecutive ordinals, exact predecessor digests and distinct scoped descendant candidates.
Sealed records retain mandatory claims, conditions, original evidence provenance, observed outcomes, outstanding obligations and cumulative resource facts.
Exact replay reconciles immutable checkpoint records without another execution or debit; conflicting and ambiguous effects remain fenced.
Terminal eligibility reauthenticates the current final checkpoint and complete, stable, satisfactory mandatory proof for the exact candidate.
The existing completion owner consumes equivalent checkpoint proof without duplicate execution while preserving distinct mandatory obligations and BR-1 through BR-6 gates.
Checkpoint completion preserves single-terminal ownership, exact terminal reconciliation and exclusion of conflicting, ambiguous or late effects.
Positive REPAIR and REMEDIATION checkpoint reuse remains blocked without independently authenticated operation-specific authority.
Native currentness checks, retained captures, durable mutation fencing and bounded accounting reject stale, interrupted, conflicting and unknown state.
Restored real-Git/native-subprocess conformance cases covering checkpoint progression, terminal reuse, coverage, replay, concurrency, interruption and adversarial authority conditions.

Committed exactly the six prescribed blobs, preserving all other base paths and legacy contracts. Documentation retains deferred activation gates. Syntax parsing passed; canonical verification was not executed.
